title: Closing the viewer's pooled readers on main blocks waiting for the server.
where: Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:311-325; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:499; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:182-188; Network/SFTPSession.swift:490-495; Network/SFTPSession.swift:186; Network/FTPConnection.swift:538-550; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:190
detail: ViewerPane.stopWork -> loaded?.source.close() -> CachedByteSource.close (:499) -> ProviderByteSource.close (:182-188) closes every idle reader. SFTP: SFTPReader.close (SFTPSession.swift:490-495) -> closeHandle (:186) sends a close request and waits for the full session timeout. FTP: FTPReader.close -> stop() -> abortTransfer (FTPConnection.swift:538-550) waits up to min(timeout,10) s, then up to 2 s per further reply. stopWork runs on main from load (every quick-view cursor move, N/P, F2, a followed link), clear, QuickViewPanel.remove and windowWillClose. Trigger: view a file on a server, the server stops answering, then press Esc, close the window or move the cursor. Duration: the session timeout (SFTP) or about 10 s (FTP), multiplied by up to one idle reader per core.
fix: Detach the reader list on main and close it on a background queue (the closeHandleLater pattern), or call interrupt() first; treat ProviderByteSource.deinit (:190) the same way.

title: ProviderByteSource.deinit closes the same readers on whichever thread drops the last reference, often main.
detail: Same blocking close as F1 (blocking call), run from deinit on whichever thread releases the last reference, which is often main.
fix: Same fix as F1: close readers on a background queue / interrupt first.

title: Multi-Rename reads the clipboard (and builds environment and titleRule) on every keystroke on main.
detail: controlTextDidChange (MultiRenameWindowController.swift:285) -> session.settings didSet -> refresh() -> makeContext (MultiRenameSession.swift:77) -> NSPasteboard.general.string(forType:) (MultiRenamePlugin.swift:55). Blocking call plus scaling. Trigger: 100 MB of text on the clipboard costs tens to hundreds of ms per key; lazily provided data from a hung application blocks without limit. The same call also builds ProcessInfo.environment and store.titleRule each time.
fix: Read the clipboard once at open, or only when the mask contains the clipboard placeholder, off main and capped in size.

title: Multi-Rename job completions do per-item URL work on main (about 0.7 s on finish, 1.5-2 s on undo at 500k).
detail: finish (:413-434): Set of 500k locationKey (measured 273 ms) plus removeAll by locationKey (317 ms), then appendUndo, panels.refresh and listChanged. About 0.7 s in total. Undo completion (:466-483): two such sets, two filters, and Set(last.flatMap { deletingLastPathComponent x2 }) (measured 816 ms). About 1.5-2 s in total.
fix: Compute gone, folders, attempted and left in the job's work closure and hand over finished values.

title: Spotlight results are extracted on main; a 2M-file query can take 10-40 s.
detail: SpotlightSearch.finished loops result(at:) and value(forAttribute:) over every result. Trigger: a query matching 2M files (an empty mask asks for kMDItemFSName == "*"). Roughly 5-20 us per result gives 10-40 s; gathering itself also runs on the main run loop. Scaling, reported as plausible.
fix: Give the NSMetadataQuery an operationQueue, extract paths there, and cap or page the results.

title: Cmd+C in Find Files results builds the whole text on main (about 1 s at 2M).
detail: handleResultKey -> copyText calls displayPath per row and joins. 536 ms measured for url.path plus join at 2M; with the provider lookup and setString of about 150 MB, roughly 1 s. Reported severity high/medium, scaling.
fix: Build the text in the background, or use lazy pasteboard data.

title: Find Files end-of-search and result actions do O(results) work on main (about 0.3 s at 2M); one folder with 1M matches arrives as a single batch.
detail: finish (:361-398): resultItems (66 ms), rebuilding rows (167 ms), a directory count (8 ms), then freeing the old array and reloadData. About 0.3 s at 2M. goToFile (:472) rebuilds resultItems on every Enter or double-click (about 66 ms); feedToListbox (:483) is O(n) before handing 2M URLs to the list service; startSearch with 'search in found' (:255) likewise. A single folder with 1M matches arrives as one batch, because flush only runs from onDirectory (:296-298).
fix: Keep counts incrementally, keep the rows at the end instead of rebuilding them, read the single item directly, and cap the batch size.

title: O(panel items) passes with a set lookup per item when 300k are marked in Find Files selectedItems, SyncSession.adopt and CompareOperands.choose (100-200 ms at 1M).
detail: Find Files selectedItems (:143-146) runs on every windowDidBecomeKey (:560), on prepare and on startSearch, only to test emptiness. SyncSession.adopt (SyncSession.swift:102) also sorts the 300k names. CompareOperands.choose (CompareContentPlugin.swift:86-98) adds a linear name search in the target panel. Roughly 100-200 ms at 1M.
fix: Find Files: use selectionCount > 0.

title: Sync window with 1M rows: rebuild, plan() and selectedRows do O(rows) work on main.
detail: rebuild() (SyncSession.swift:209-238) runs on every Show toggle, header click and finish: a dictionary grouped by directory string, an optional sort, positions, and SyncSummary(rows). Estimated 0.2-0.5 s, followed by reloadData. synchronize() -> plan() (:354, SyncPlan.swift:32-52) copies all visible rows and builds the plan with a small array allocation per row; estimated 0.3-1 s before the dialog appears. selectedRows (SyncWindowController.swift:345) is rebuilt on every key press in the table.
fix: Cache per-directory groups and summary counts, build the plan in the background, compute selectedRows only in the branches that use it.

title: Multi-Rename per-keystroke O(rows) work on main at 500k rows, with no debounce (50-150 ms per key); other O(rows) actions.
detail: refresh() maps rows to entries (MultiRenameSession.swift:90; 18 ms measured for a comparable copy). update() (MultiRenameWindowController.swift:307-341) runs counts over all rows and reloadData, once at the keystroke and again when the preview lands, after apply (MultiRenameSession.swift:111-119) has written 500k names. Roughly 50-150 ms per key. The preview itself is correctly in the background and cancellable, but there is no debounce. Shift+Up/Down (:201-207), nextStep, Edit names (:285-291, a 500k-line modal text view) and loadNames(fromText:) (up to 32 MB split on main) are O(rows) too.
fix: Debounce about 100 ms, keep an entries array alongside the rows, and have the preview return its counts.

title: Multi-Rename undo history is JSON-decoded on main at first window open; a 500k-item run is persisted and decoded next session (est. 1-3 s).
detail: update() -> canUndo -> RenameStore.undoHistory (:134-138) JSON-decodes [[RenamedItem]] at the first window open. persistedRuns (:166-175) always keeps the newest run, whatever its size, so a 500k-item run is stored and decoded next session; estimated 1-3 s. The write hop (:185-189) hands a multi-megabyte Data to the settings store on main. Reported severity medium/high, scaling, plausible.
fix: Decode lazily in the background and store only a count for canUndo.

title: Compare recomputes on main when both files total under 20,000 lines (est. 0.3-1 s per option change, edit, copy, undo or resync).
detail: CompareSession.recompute runs CompareLoader.text inline when both files total under 20,000 lines; the diff is then exact (Myers.exactBelow = 20,000), and it calls Parallel.map from main (CompareLoader.swift:98). Trigger: two unrelated 10k-line files, on every option checkbox, cell edit, copy, undo or resync. Estimated 0.3-1 s; more with long lines, since up to 128 MB is normalised. Code path confirmed, time estimated.
fix: Always go to the background, or gate on bytes and elapsed time.

title: Compare cells lay out whole lines, so multi-megabyte lines take seconds on main.
detail: viewFor builds an attributed string of the entire line, and TextDiff.inline copies both whole lines to UTF-16 before truncating to 4,096. Trigger: a file of up to 128 MB with multi-megabyte lines (minified JSON); layout of one such cell takes seconds. Reported severity medium/high, scaling, plausible.
fix: Truncate the displayed text to a few thousand characters and take a prefix before Array(utf16).

title: Viewer completions do large work on main: print, copy selection, HTML, RTF, first image draw.
detail: printContent (:650-654): sizeToFit lays out up to 2 MB of text; estimated 0.5-3 s. copySelection (:466-467): setString of up to 64 MB, or about 192 MB as hex; 0.1-0.5 s. show(html:) (ViewerPane.swift:584): loadHTMLString with up to 1 GB (wholeFileLimit). RTF view (RichViews.swift:299): setAttributedString with up to 1 GB. First image draw (ImageCanvasView.swift:173,187): a frame of up to 8192^2 drawn with high interpolation until the scaled bitmap is ready; estimated 0.1-0.4 s. Scaling, plausible.
fix: Lower the limits for HTML and RTF, load HTML from a temporary file, and draw at low quality until the bitmap exists.

title: CompareSession.edit copies the whole lines array on each edit, and 20 undo levels each keep a full copy.
detail: The undo snapshot shares the array, so each edit copies it. With millions of lines that is about 0.1-0.3 s per edit. Reported severity low/medium, scaling, confirmed.
fix: Store deltas.

title: Modal run loops (open/save/page-layout panels and kernel.ui form/inform/pick from completions) run on main.
detail: NSOpenPanel / NSSavePanel / NSPageLayout runModal (ViewerPane+Actions.swift:537,547,602) and kernel.ui.form / inform / pick from completions (sync finish, compare finish, rename finish). Each is raised once per operation; none can be raised repeatedly from a flood.

title: Viewer text path is off main and bounded.
detail: Every read, index build, row fetch, reveal, search, copy read, HTML strip and decode runs on workQueue, fetchQueue or a global queue, with generation checks. Rows are always cut at the column limit, so a 10 GB single line becomes bounded rows. The TextRowIndex, CachedByteSource and DiskBlockCache locks are never held across provider I/O (only a local pread/pwrite of at most 256 KB). Scrolling is O(1) plus an asynchronous fetch.

title: CTLine drawing cost is small.
detail: Measured 60 CTLines of 16,384 characters at about 5 ms, so drawing a page is cheap even at the widest setting.

title: Flooding is throttled.
detail: Find Files batches, duplicate status, sync progress, viewer search progress and rename job progress are all time-throttled (10-20 Hz), and stale generations are dropped.

title: Compare load, large recompute and find are in the background.
detail: Load, large recompute and find are in the background; block(containing:) bisects; the inline cache is capped.

title: Multi-Rename preview, sorts and undo writes are off main.
detail: Preview and long sorts are in the background and cancellable; large undo writes are encoded off main.

title: Find Files uses insertRows and an early-exit updateButtons.
detail: insertRows rather than reloadData per batch; updateButtons exits early.

title: No blocking file or provider calls on main in the five plugins.
detail: No FileManager, stat or provider item/list/volume call was found on main in these five plugins. The only ones on main are text-only (displayPath, location(from:), capabilities(for:)).

title: Not covered: SearchForm field handling, saved searches and history sizes.
detail: Only grepped.

title: Not covered: ViewerSearch, HTMLText, hex/binary row builders, MediaView, and per-key handleKey / menuEntries cost.
detail: Not examined.

title: Not covered: sync and rename executors and SyncComparison.
detail: Background; only their main-thread hops were checked.

title: Not covered: kernel and other plugins' costs.
detail: PanelModel.hasOperandFile / operands, PanelSet.refresh with very many changed folders (called from sync, rename and compare completions), the settings store's set cost, and FileListService.show with 2M URLs.

title: Nothing was profiled in the running app.
detail: Apart from the one micro-benchmark, all durations are estimates.

title: watch() runs realpath, FSEventStreamCreate and Start on the caller's (main) thread, so a stalled SMB/NFS mount freezes the UI on any location change.
detail: Category: freeze. watch() runs realpath() on every directory, then FSEventStreamCreate with WatchRoot (which opens each path) and FSEventStreamStart, all on the caller's thread. The caller is PanelCoordinator.updateWatchers (main-thread only, runs on every location change). Trigger: the right panel shows a folder on an SMB/NFS share that has stalled; the user navigates in the left panel; updateWatchers re-resolves both directories and realpath on the dead mount blocks main with no timeout. Also: VirtualFolders passes up to 512 folders per call, so one call can be 512 realpaths; which thread that call runs on was not checked.
basis: read (confirmed by code path; the stall was not simulated)
fix: Have LocalFileSystem.watch return the token at once and do resolve/create/start on the watcher's own serial queue, with stop serialised on the same queue. Also skip re-resolving directories whose locationKey has not changed.

title: places() computes a fresh one-second deadline on every call while knownPlaces is nil, so main freezes 1 s per call with a stalled mount at launch.
detail: Category: freeze. The comment says only the first question waits; the code waits on every call until the first read finishes. Reached on main from DriveBarView.rebuild (at launch and on every mount notification), the volume menu and NavigationPlugin. Trigger: launch with a stalled network mount; readPlaces() (mountedVolumeURLs plus per-volume resourceValues) hangs, and each main-thread call freezes the UI for a full second, indefinitely. Related: even on a healthy machine the first call at launch blocks main until the read is done, against the protocol's 'must answer at once'. If readPlaces hangs, isReadingPlaces stays true forever and the list never refreshes again.
basis: read (confirmed by reading; that mountedVolumeURLs hangs on a dead mount is plausible)
fix: Never wait in places(); return fixedPlaces() until the first read lands and announce the result (see finding 3). Give the reader a watchdog that clears isReadingPlaces, and read volumes individually so one bad volume does not hold up the rest.

title: Nothing tells clients when the places list has been re-read, so the drive bar shows stale volumes.
detail: Category: correctness. DriveBarView rebuilds on the same NSWorkspace mount notification that only starts the provider's background refresh, so it gets the old list. Trigger: plug in a disk; the drive bar does not show it until some later rebuild; after an unmount the stale button stays.
fix: Post a placesDidChange notification on main when knownPlaces actually changes, and have the bar observe that instead of NSWorkspace.

title: DirectoryWatcher has no client-side coalescing; each FSEvents callback becomes one main-thread onChange, about 450/s under load.
detail: Category: performance. Each FSEvents callback becomes one queue.async to main, and under load FSEvents flushes far more often than the 0.5 s latency. Measured: four writers creating and deleting files in the watched folder gave 2,696 main-thread onChange calls in 6 s (about 450 per second). Flooding only a sub-sub-folder still gave 115 calls in 6 s, because MustScanSubDirs marks every watched folder as changed. Trigger: a build or npm install anywhere below a folder a panel shows keeps the panel re-listing continuously; the shell serialises reloads so they do not pile up, but they never stop. Also: because streams are recursive, watching ~ or / bridges every event path in the subtree to a Swift String on the utility queue.
fix: Keep a pending set in Watch and deliver at most one report per interval (trailing-edge timer, 0.3-1 s, longer after MustScanSubDirs). Consider kFSEventStreamCreateFlagIgnoreSelf.

title: A loaded tab file has no tab-count limit; 81,512 tabs from 1 MiB make restore O(n^2) on main and hang the app.
detail: Category: freeze. A 1 MiB file parses to 81,512 tabs (measured, 0.09 s), and restore then calls insertTab once per tab on main, each firing onChange -> tabsChanged, which does work proportional to the tab count. Trigger: the user loads a crafted or corrupt .tab file. O(n^2) on main, and replace adds a firstIndex plus closeTab per old tab.
basis: measured (parse count confirmed; O(n^2) UI cost read, not timed)
fix: Cap tabs per side (a few hundred) and caption length. Add a batch insert to PanelTabs that fires onChange once.

title: append opens with O_WRONLY and no O_NONBLOCK and checks S_IFREG after the open, so a FIFO with no reader hangs the job thread forever.
detail: Category: freeze. On a FIFO with no reader the open blocks forever and cannot be cancelled. read() has the same problem through FileHandle(forReadingFrom:). Trigger: Resume/Append onto a destination name that is a FIFO or a link to one, or view/stream-copy a FIFO where the caller's isSpecial check raced. Related: copyMetadata(from: plain, to: fifo) also blocked in the experiment (copyfile opening the destination, line 597); indicative only because the FIFO still had a reader thread blocked on it from earlier cases in the same run.
basis: reproduced (append confirmed; read inferred from POSIX FIFO semantics, not cleanly isolated; copyMetadata observed once)
fix: Open with O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC, fstat, reject non-regular files, then clear O_NONBLOCK with fcntl. In copyMetadata, refuse when the destination's lstat says it is neither regular, directory nor link.

title: Every symlink and dotted folder in a listing gets an uncancellable stat/resourceValues/getattrlist, so a link into a dead share hangs the listing and pins pool threads.
detail: Category: freeze/threading. Every symlink in a listing gets a following stat(), and every dotted folder gets resourceValues or getattrlist, on the listing thread or inside Parallel.map workers. None can be cancelled. Trigger: a local folder (such as ~) contains a link into a dead share or an autofs path; the listing never completes (the flag is only looked at between buffers). Each stuck call also pins a ParallelPool thread for good (the pool is capped at four times its width).
basis: inferred (plausible; code path certain, hang not simulated)
fix: Do not resolve link targets inline. Deliver links unresolved and resolve them lazily, or on a separate bounded queue with a deadline. At minimum skip resolution on non-local volumes (statfs f_flags of the directory) and check the flag per entry.

title: lockedCopies keeps every locked copy forever, so remove()/move() silently unlock and delete user-locked files; the 4,096-entry wipe also drops in-flight temp entries.
detail: Category: correctness (lock bypass). lockedCopies also records copies that keep their final name: every locked destination of copy() and every locked item touched by copyMetadata, folders included. Nothing ever forgets them. For the rest of the session remove() and move() silently unlock and delete or rename those user-locked files with no 'this item is locked' step. Confirmed: copy of a uchg file followed by remove(dst) succeeded; copyMetadata onto a folder followed by move succeeded. Second problem: at 4,096 entries the table is wiped (removeAll, line 478), which also drops entries for in-flight temporary files of other workers; their rename then fails with EPERM and remove fails too. FileJob.discard (FileJob.swift:738) retries after unlocking via setAttributes, so cleanup still works, but the item fails.
fix: Make the allowance explicit and scoped: e.g. copy returns a token, or the caller passes allowLocked to the single rename/remove of its own temp; or the entry expires on first use and after a short TTL. Never bulk-clear; evict the oldest.

title: write() creates files 0644 and applies the source permissions only at close by path, exposing 0600 content and allowing a symlink race.
detail: Category: security. write() creates files with mode 0644 (confirmed); source permissions are applied only at close, by path. FileManager.setAttributes(ofItemAtPath:) follows symlinks. Exposure: stream-copying a 0600 file (archive or server to disk, or a followed link) leaves its content world-readable in the destination folder for the whole transfer, and permanently if the transfer fails with partial files kept. Race: in a shared-writable destination, swapping the just-closed temp for a symlink makes the chmod/utimes land on another file of the user.
fix: open(..., 0o600), then fchmod/futimens on the descriptor before closing it; add O_CLOEXEC.

title: setAttributes unlocks the link itself but changes mode and date through fm.setAttributes, which follows the link and alters the target.
detail: Category: correctness. Confirmed: calling it on a symlink changed the target's mode to 777 and its mtime. Trigger: Change Attributes on a selection containing links, or a job carrying attributes onto a copied link, alters files outside the tree being worked on. Also: the unlock is not rolled back if the later step fails.
fix: Use fchmodat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and utimensat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW), or setattrlist with FSOPT_NOFOLLOW. Decide explicitly whether links are skipped.

title: Sort fallback and display filters run synchronously on main (0.5 s sort, 0.2 s filter per million entries).
detail: Reported severity LOW-MEDIUM, freeze. Sort: when the list changed while a background sort ran, the fallback is model.setSort(order), a synchronous sort on main; measured 0.5 s for one million entries, on top of the model's filter and index work. With a busy folder (finding 4 bumps listVersion constantly, as do computed sizes at PanelModel.swift:705) the stale path is the normal path. Filters: apply always calls the synchronous model.setFilter, about 0.2 s of single-threaded matching per million entries on main. The kernel's off-thread PanelModel.filtered / setFilter(_:prefiltered:listVersion:) path is not used.
fix: On a stale result, re-dispatch the sort with the new snapshot (a loop keyed by pendingOrders). Route filters through the prefiltered path above the same threshold.

title: A sort set by another route while a background sort is pending is overwritten when the background result lands.
detail: Category: correctness. pendingOrders[id] == order still holds, so setSort(order) runs. Trigger: a header click, or tab restore in FolderTabsPlugin.swift:266, during a pending background sort.
fix: If model.sort != from, drop the result.

title: TabFile writes values unescaped, so a newline in a folder name or caption injects lines (and edge spaces do not round-trip).
detail: Category: security/correctness. Confirmed: a tab at /tmp/a\n0_path=sftp://evil.example/ with caption t\n1_path=/etc reads back as tabs sftp://evil.example and /etc. Trigger: a folder with such a name arrives in an extracted archive; the user saves tabs while in it and loads them later. Also: leading and trailing spaces in a path do not round-trip, because lines are trimmed.
fix: Refuse or escape CR/LF in paths and captions on write; do not trim the value side.

title: A UTF-8 BOM makes TabFile reject the first section header; UTF-16 tab files fail through the lossy decode.
detail: Category: correctness. TabFile(text: "\u{FEFF}[activetabs]...") returns nil (confirmed), so the user sees 'The file holds no tabs'. UTF-16 files, which Windows tools write, fail the same way through the lossy decode at FolderTabsPlugin.swift:410.
fix: Strip the BOM; detect UTF-16 by its BOM.

title: Tab paths are read with fileSystems.location(from:), so an untrusted .tab file can make the app connect to any scheme/host or trigger automounts.
detail: Category: security. A tab file can name any scheme or path (sftp://host/..., /net/host/...). The active tab of each side is opened immediately. Trigger: loading an untrusted .tab file makes the app connect to a host of the file's choosing or trigger automounts.
basis: inferred (plausible; depends on what the Network plugin does without a prompt)
fix: Ask for confirmation when a loaded file contains non-local locations.

title: move(replacing: true) between two hard links of the same file returns success while the source still exists.
detail: Category: correctness. rename(2) is a no-op there. A Move job reports success and nothing moved.
fix: When replacing, compare dev/ino of both names and unlink the source if they match.

title: copy() hands anything that is not a regular file to fm.copyItem, so a directory is copied with no progress and no cancellation.
detail: Category: correctness/freeze. If a caller passes a directory, the whole tree is copied with no progress and no cancellation (confirmed: zero progress calls). The contract says 'one file or link' but nothing enforces it.
fix: Allow only S_IFLNK (via symlink/copyfile with NOFOLLOW) and throw for directories and special files.

title: createDirectory succeeds silently when the directory exists or is a symlink to a directory.
detail: Category: correctness. Both confirmed. Callers cannot tell 'created' from 'was there', and a tree copy writes through a pre-existing link.
fix: mkdir the leaf yourself and report EEXIST; let the caller decide about merging; lstat the leaf.

title: Full listing delivers an entry whose bulk attributes and lstat both failed as a zero-byte 1970 non-file, while the lean entries(of:) drops it.
detail: Category: correctness. A deleted-meanwhile entry is still delivered by the full listing.
fix: Drop it in both.

title: String(cString:) repairs invalid UTF-8 names with U+FFFD, so the item's URL names a nonexistent file on NFS/FUSE volumes.
detail: Category: correctness. On volumes that allow such names (NFS, some FUSE) open/copy/delete fail with ENOENT.
fix: Detect the repair and either keep the raw bytes (percent-encoded URL built from bytes) or mark the item unreadable.

title: totalSize checks the cancel flag once per directory, not per buffer, and copy does not pass COPYFILE_DATA_SPARSE.
detail: Category: performance. A million-entry folder is read to the end after Cancel. Also copy does not pass COPYFILE_DATA_SPARSE, so a cross-volume copy of a sparse image is written out in full and can fill the target disk.

title: spareSpace is keyed by mount-point path, so a different volume remounted at the same path inherits the old spare figure.
detail: Category: correctness. spareSpace is only dropped when a re-measure fails. After eject and re-mount of a different volume at the same path (/Volumes/Untitled), the old spare figure is added to the new volume's free space until the next measurement (3 s or more).
fix: Key by f_fsid, or store it and compare.

title: If FSEventStreamCreate fails, watched is already set, so a later watch() with the same folders returns early and never retries.
detail: Category: correctness.
fix: Set watched only after a successful start.

title: No raw open uses O_CLOEXEC and no syscall retries EINTR.
detail: Category: leak/robustness. Affects open on interruptible NFS, getattrlistbulk, ftruncate.

title: Listing a dataless iCloud/File Provider directory materialises it and blocks with no timeout; totalSize over iCloud Drive materialises every folder.
detail: Category: freeze. File contents are never downloaded, since nothing opens files.
fix: Consider setiopolicy_np(IOPOL_TYPE_VFS_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES, ...OFF) for size and tree walks, and surface EDEADLK as 'not downloaded'.

title: pasteboard.string(forType:) runs on main in Go to Path from Clipboard; a lazy or huge clipboard blocks.
detail: Category: freeze. A lazily provided or very large clipboard blocks for as long as the owning app takes.

title: readPlaces calls (mountedVolumeURLs, resourceValues, fileExists) have no timeout; a stuck read blocks refresh forever.
detail: Blocking-calls table: reaching thread is a global queue; timeout or cancel: none; stuck forever blocks refresh.

title: open + getattrlistbulk in listing, job and pool threads is cancelled only between buffers, and not at all inside totalSize's loop.
detail: Blocking-calls table: flag checked between buffers only (not at all inside totalSize's loop).

title: stat/lstat per link or failed entry on listing and pool threads has no timeout or cancel.
detail: Blocking-calls table: none.

title: resourceValues(.isPackage) and getattrlist on listing and pool threads have no timeout or cancel; contentsOfDirectory fallback on the listing thread has none either.
detail: Blocking-calls table: none for both rows.

title: fileExists loop, resourceValues and statfs in volume(of:) run on the listing thread, utility queue and jobs with no timeout.
detail: Blocking-calls table: reaching thread is the listing thread (Listing.swift:81), utility queue, jobs; timeout or cancel: none.

title: measureSpareSpace on the utility queue has no timeout and isMeasuring stays set if it hangs.
detail: Blocking-calls table: none; isMeasuring stays set.

title: FileHandle open/read/write/close and open/fstat/ftruncate/lseek in append on job threads have no interrupt() on Reader or Writer; append checks the flag once.
detail: Blocking-calls table.

title: copyfile (539, 597) and fm.copyItem (508) are cancellable only through the progress callback between chunks; none for metadata or copyItem.
detail: Blocking-calls table: job threads.

title: rename/renamex_np, unlink/rmdir, lchflags, setxattr/getxattr, setattrlist, fm.setAttributes, trashItem and createDirectory on job threads have no timeout or cancel.
detail: Blocking-calls table. The report found no main-thread path into blocking storage calls within its scope apart from the first two rows (watch and places).

title: unlockOwnCopy has a small lstat -> lchflags window under lockedLock.
detail: Shared-mutable-state table: lock sufficient; table semantics wrong (finding 8); small lstat->lchflags window in unlockOwnCopy. The swap was reasoned about, not reproduced.

title: Places state is lock-protected correctly (wait policy wrong).
detail: knownPlaces, placesRead, isReadingPlaces, placesChangedMeanwhile under placesCondition: locking correct; wait policy wrong (finding 2).

title: mountObservers is written in init and read in deinit.
detail: Fine.

title: packageExtensions under packageLock is sufficient.
detail: packageLock is never held across syscalls; benign duplicate asks.

title: spareSpace under spareLock is sufficient.
detail: Released around measuring; first-question race only duplicates a 15 ms measure; stale key is finding 22.

title: DirectoryWatcher.stream/watch/watched are unsynchronised but have a single owner.
detail: Fine while each watcher has one owner.

title: Watch.stopped under NSLock is sufficient.
Watch lifetime is retained by the stream's context.
detail: Sound.

title: ViewOptions applied/pendingOrders and FolderTabs closedTabs are main-thread only.
detail: Fine; ObjectIdentifier reuse is guarded by the weak-model check, or by the closure retaining the model.

title: FTPReader.close() interrupts outside stateLock, so it can cut a recycled connection now used by another thread (BUG 1).
detail: Medium-low. Path 1: close() captures running and reading == true under stateLock, unlocks, then calls running?.connection.interrupt() at FS:710. Path 2: the reading thread hits end of file: setActive(nil) FS:644 -> finishTransfer -> release FS:646 puts the connection in idle. A third thread pops it at FS:216. Interleaving: close() unlocks; the reader finishes and releases; thread X acquires the connection; close() then cuts X's control stream. X sees a spurious connectionLost, which is not retried for mkdir/delete/rename (commandMayHaveRun) or for uploads.
fix: Call interrupt() while holding stateLock, re-reading active, exactly as interrupt() does at FS:696-698.

title: FTPReader.close() from another thread races with seek() (BUG 2).
detail: seek never calls begin(), so close() sees isReading == false. It then runs stop() and writes atEnd (FS:713-714) while the owner reads and writes atEnd/position/active unlocked. Outside the kernel contract (which only requires interrupt to be concurrent-safe) but inside the class's own documented promise (FS:573).
fix: Bracket seek with begin()/end().

title: Keep-alive pulls all stale idle FTP connections at once and pings them serially (up to 5 s each), so a foreground command can wait N x 5 s (BUG 3).
detail: Low-medium, responsiveness. They still count in total, so a foreground command at FS:221 waits up to N x 5 s on a silently dead link. isAlive() (NOOP, up to 5 s, no cancellation) runs outside any lock, serially per stale connection.
fix: Ping one at a time, or do not count pinged connections against the limit.

title: No 421 retry for the second 'first' login thread (BUG 4).
detail: Two threads both read isFirst == true (FS:110). The second opens after the first succeeded, but the 421 retry at FS:164 requires !isFirst. On a one-connection server it fails instead of retrying.
fix: Re-read hasConnected after taking loginLock.

title: SFTPSession.disconnect() during a login does not stop it; the channel is stored on a closed session and ssh lives on (BUG 5).
detail: SS:162-169 sees channel == nil. open() then stores the channel and sets hasConnected (SS:127-129) on a closed session. The ssh process lives until the session is deallocated.
fix: Check isClosed at SS:127 and close created.

title: resolveLinksLater has no bound per session; link-heavy listings hold command connections up to 20 s each and can open login dialogs from a background task (BUG 6).
detail: Medium, responsiveness. There is one task per listing with unresolved links. Each holds a command connection for up to 20 s and counts against parallelConnections, so three link-heavy listings can stall the next foreground listing. It can also open a login dialog from a background task (FS:169). Also an unbounded wait in acquire with a nil flag (FS:426).
fix: One serial resolver per session with coalescing, yielding the connection between probes.

title: Potential deadlock if outside code calls a connecting provider method on main while a background thread holds loginLock/connectLock across askUser (main.sync).

Main: provider.item/list/read/write -> FS.acquire -> openConnection -> loginLock.lock() (FS:113), or SS.open -> connectLock (SS:84). Background: holds that lock inside askCredentials/askSecret -> Kernel.askUser -> DispatchQueue.main.sync. The only outside callers checked (FileOperationsPlugin.swift:507 and :552) are inside jobs.run work; the rest left for the whole-program pass.

title: Job-completion thread (main or not) for NC.connect failure completion was assumed, not checked.
Tree scan issues one outline.reloadItem per scanned folder, stalling the window (up to 2000 reloads = 1.6-1.8 s per turn).
detail: Scaling/flooding. Path: scanner batch -> DispatchQueue.main.async (:274) -> linkWaiting() -> outline.reloadItem(node, reloadChildren: true) for every finished level whose node has a row. linkBudget (2000) counts linked nodes, with a minimum of 1 per level, so one turn can make up to 2000 reloadItem calls. Measured: 2000 x reloadItem(child, reloadChildren: true) = 1.6-1.8 s, independent of row count (headless NSOutlineView). Trigger: first scan or F2 rescan while an expanded folder shows thousands of subfolders, e.g. reveal expanded a node_modules. With 1M visible subfolders this is about 500 consecutive 1.6 s turns.

title: OpenArchive.capabilities takes a lock held across syscalls and O(n) work, so every isWritable validation can block main (lock).
detail: Path: validation tick or menu open -> any isWritable closure -> FileSystemRegistry.capabilities(for:) -> ArchiveFileSystem.capabilities(for:) -> OpenArchive.capabilities -> locked {}. Background holders: isCurrent() (:476-483) does FileSignature.of(localURL.path) (a stat) under the lock; install (:1268-1280) does a stat and a rename under it; rebase (:1313) re-reads the whole central directory (load()) under it; takeSnapshot (:1105) sorts all entries under it; finishWrite (:843-851) calls environment.hasRoom (a volume query) under it. Trigger and duration: a panel inside a ZIP on a stalled mount: 30-600 s on the next tick; a 1M-entry ZIP during a flush or a re-read after an external change: estimated 0.5-several s per occurrence. VirtualFileSystem inherits this for a branch of a zip.
fix: Publish capabilities as a lock-free atomic snapshot, updated wherever format, hasDuplicates or fetchedCopy change. Move the stat, rename and load out of the lock.

Callers outside scope: Navigation (cd), Places, Selection, FolderTabs, CommandRunner, Sync and Compare call the same registry method; their thread was not checked. Duration: microseconds normally; the mount timeout on a stalled volume.

detail: place() calls writeObjects with one NSURL per item. Measured 3.2 s for 100k and linear (about 32 us per URL), so about 9.6 s for 300k, plus operands().
fix: Cap the count or ask first; build one pasteboard item with a file-list type; at minimum show progress.

title: Paste of 100k URLs takes 1.1 s readObjects + 139 ms isSameLocation filter + 0.1-0.2 s completion on main.
detail: files() -> readObjects at :142 measured 1.1 s. isSameLocation filter at :158 measured 139 ms. The transfer completion at FileOperationsPlugin.swift:362-364 adds about 0.1-0.2 s (estimate).

title: Verify Checksums on ordinary files builds a FileMask and compiles an NSRegularExpression per item on main (about 1.3-1.5 s at 300k) and reads the pasteboard string.
detail: isChecksumFile builds a FileMask per item: measured 286 ms. checksumInName compiles an NSRegularExpression per item: measured 773 ms. Total with operands() about 1.3-1.5 s, before the 'Please select only...' alert. It also reads the general pasteboard string on main at :297; that blocks if the clipboard owner supplies the text lazily and is slow.
fix: Hoist the mask and the regex out of the loop; do the classification in the job.

title: Copy/Move/Delete start does operands() (up to 441 ms) and delete adds capabilities allSatisfy (35-50 ms local, est. 1-1.5 s in a zip or list).
detail: Start: operands() only, up to 441 ms. delete adds items.allSatisfy { capabilities(for:) } (:327), about 35-50 ms on local files. Inside a zip or a list every call takes locks and parses a URL: estimated 1-1.5 s, and F2 applies.

title: Copy/Move/Delete completion computes names(of:among:) (387 ms) and model.deselect (97 ms) in one main-queue block (about 0.5 s).
detail: Completion.
fix: Compute the names on the job thread before returning; the completion then only applies a ready set.

title: Pack completion builds Set<URL> and runs contains on main (183 ms) plus deselect.
Change Attributes and Create Link completions do per-item parentPaths/locationKey work on main (est. 0.3-0.5 s at 300k).
detail: The closest measurement is 280 ms for parentPaths at 300k; the extra locationKey per item puts these at an estimated 0.3-0.5 s.

title: Create separate checksum files passes up to 300k folders to panels.refresh, which compares each against both panels (est. 0.8 s or more).
Add to Download List calls displayPath per item on main (est. 0.5-1.5 s for 300k remote items).
Copy Path of Each File (280 ms) and Copy Names with Path (88 ms) run on main, plus operands() and a large setString.
detail: Both plus operands(), then setString of 20 MB or more (estimated tens of ms; 100 MB measured 16 ms).

title: LocalFileSystem.places() can wait 1 s on main per call while knownPlaces is nil.
detail: Blocking call. It waits up to 1 s on the condition while knownPlaces == nil. The comment assumes only the first call waits. If the first background readPlaces() (mountedVolumeURLs with resource values) is stuck on a dead mount present at launch, knownPlaces stays nil. Callers: DriveBarView.rebuild and PanelViewController.swift:916; each call blocks a full second for as long as the read is stuck.
fix: Wait only once (set a 'waited' flag), or seed knownPlaces with fixedPlaces() in init.

title: Archives stop() flushes every archive synchronously on main at quit (seconds to minutes; unbounded on a stalled mount).
detail: Reported medium to high; blocking call, quit only. Path: applicationWillTerminate -> kernel.shutdown() on main -> ArchivesPlugin.stop -> store.flushAll(). Rewrites or uploads every archive with pending changes. Rewrites are delayed up to 60 s by idleDelay, so a multi-GB ZIP edited shortly before Cmd-Q can freeze for seconds to minutes.
fix: Do this in applicationShouldTerminate with .terminateLater, a background flush and a progress sheet.

title: FileOperationsPlugin.stop -> OperationLog.flush() does a queue.sync on main at quit; blocks if the log is on a stalled volume.
detail: Quit only.
fix: Same: flush in applicationShouldTerminate with .terminateLater.

title: NetworkPlugin.stop -> disconnectAll sends QUIT with a 2 s write timeout per idle FTP connection and up to 0.5 s per SFTP channel on main at quit.
detail: Quit only.
fix: Same.

title: Keychain calls (SecItemCopyMatching/Delete/Add) run on main in several network commands.
detail: Blocking call, plausible. Callers on main: NetworkCommands.edit and showConnections (password lookup when the editor opens, set on OK, copy on duplicate), the Disconnect 'save?' path, and askCredentials inside askUser. Duration: normally 5-50 ms; unbounded while securityd shows an unlock or permission prompt. Sound part: the login path reads the password on the connecting thread.
fix: Run Keychain calls in a job or on a utility queue.

title: Create Link joins every failure into one ui.inform detail; 300k lines make NSAlert lay out about 20 MB of text.
detail: Modal/scaling, plausible. Links into a read-only target for 300k items give 300k lines (the join itself measured 11 ms). NSAlert must lay out about 20 MB of text; estimated several seconds or more inside a modal.
fix: Cap at about 20 lines plus '... and N more', as FileJob and ArchiveCommands.summary already do.

title: ListRun skipped lines are unbounded in an alert, and the method recurses once per unsupported line (stack overflow risk).
detail: Same pattern as Create Link alert, usually small. The method recurses once per unsupported line (:450), so a very long list of unsupported lines risks a stack overflow.
fix: Cap at about 20 lines plus '... and N more'.

title: countDirectoryContents enabled closure scans all 1M items (items.contains(where: \.isFolder)) when the folder holds only files (est. 2-5 ms per validation).
detail: Scaling; runs on every Files-menu or context-menu validation.
fix: Keep a folder count in PanelModel.totals.

title: model.selection.count > 1 builds a Set<String> of all marks (22 ms at 300k) in enabled closures and unpack.
fix: Use selectionCount.

title: nameContext reads the pasteboard string on main when the typed name contains [X.
Verify completion does report.text and setSelection(names:) O(rows) on main (low to medium for a ~1M-line checksum file).
Paste enabled closure costs 55 ms on the first call after 100k URLs land on the pasteboard.
detail: canReadObject(NSURL) measured 55 ms on the first call after 100k URLs land on the pasteboard, about 0.01 ms after; 0.09 ms with 100 MB of text; types only, never the data.

title: saveDetails (two), setAttributes and editComment, and the file-operation enabled closures inherit the OpenArchive.capabilities lock stall (F2) inside a zip.
detail: From the enabled-closure inventory.

title: Progress reporting is throttled at the source.
detail: FileJob progressInterval = 0.04 (FileOperationsPlugin.swift:185, enforced at FileJob.swift:1472-1474), so at most 25 reports/s regardless of worker count. ToolRun.advance allows at most 20/s with a try-lock; forced reports are per part or phase, not per block. Archive testing ticks at 10 Hz. The failures list is capped at 20. How monitor.report reaches main is the shell's side.

title: Questions from jobs are modal one at a time and user-driven.
detail: All go through monitor.ask or kernel.askUser. Compare-contents hashing runs on the job thread between dialogs. The archive failure alert is shown once per distinct message.

title: Transfer setup runs on the job thread.
detail: TargetSpec.parse, FileJob construction, target-folder creation and the per-item URL mapping all run inside makeJob. The dialog texts are O(1) ('Copy N file(s) to'), with no joining of names.

title: Operation log writes go to their own queue in 0.25 s bursts.
detail: flushSoon is asynchronous.

title: DirectoryWatcher delivery is bounded.
detail: FSEvents latency is 0.5 s, so 5,000 events/s arrive as about two callbacks per second. Sifting happens on the stream queue, and there is at most one main.async per callback, carrying at most the watched directories.

title: Network connect, list, mount, eject and disconnect run in jobs or on a utility queue.
detail: FTP and SFTP state locks are never held during I/O. center.connected and capabilities(for:) are short. There is no DNS on main.

title: FileProperties attribute reads, properties, space calculation, comment load/save and link creation run in jobs.
detail: Content columns (LocalInfo, CommentStore, whose condition.wait is at Descript.swift:193) are evaluated by the shell's ColumnValueStore on a utility queue, not main.

title: Entering and listing a 1M-entry archive runs in the background.
detail: The Parallel.map calls, semaphores, Background.run and waitUntilExit in Codecs, Unpacker and FileJob are all on job threads. The store's table lock is short.

title: Paste enabled closure looks at types only, never data.
Not covered: bodies of FileJob, Packer, Unpacker, ZipFormat, Tar, Codecs, Transcoding, Hashes, SplitCombine, SFTPChannel and NetStream beyond threading entry points.
detail: They run on job threads.

title: Not covered: shell-side ProgressJobService.report/ask, PanelModel.setComputedSizes / setSelected(names:) / deselect redraw cost, SettingsStore implementation, ui.form / pickRow.
detail: Each settings.flag is a JSON decode; about 25 reads per transfer start.

title: No live test against a stalled mount or a hung pasteboard owner.
detail: F1-F3, F6 and F7 durations are from reading the code. Cross-process pasteboard costs may exceed the in-process figures measured.

title: Other plugins' main-thread calls to fileSystems.location(from:) (F3 root cause) need checking by their reviewers.
Deadlock at quit: main blocks on flushLock (L5) while a timer thread holding L5 uploads to a network provider and asks the user via main.sync (BUG 1).
detail: Archive on a network provider. Path T (GCD utility): timerFired :752 -> flush :1045 takes L5 -> upload :1362 provider.write(temporary...) (or :1373 move, :1379 item) -> the network connection asks -> Kernel.askUser -> DispatchQueue.main.sync. Path M (main): applicationWillTerminate -> Kernel.shutdown -> stop() :97 -> flushAll ArchiveFileSystem.swift:185 -> flush :1045 -> flushLock.lock(). Interleaving: M blocks on L5 first, then T's connection asks. applicationShouldTerminate cancels jobs only (Shell.swift:103-105); the timer is not a job. Both in-scope paths read; the network side is confirmed only as far as environment.askCredentials/askToTrust/askSecret -> kernel.askUser (NetworkCommands.swift:44-78); not traced into the provider's write path. Even without a question, M freezes for the whole rewrite or upload: upload makes a private CancellationFlag() (:1361) that nobody can set.
basis: read (in-scope paths confirmed; network side partly traced)
fix: Never take L5 on main. Run stop()'s flush on a background thread with a cancellable flag while main pumps a modal 'Saving archives...' sheet, or flush in applicationShouldTerminate before replying. Give OpenArchive a shutdown flag that timer flushes honour.

title: Store eviction races with a writer: an archive can be detached after resolve and get pending changes that commit/flushAll never see (BUG 2; silent no-op commit, possible data loss on move).
detail: Reported Medium-Low, narrow window. The comment at ArchiveFileSystem.swift:155-157 ('nobody can start a change between the look and the removal') is false: archive(at:) returns the archive after L3 is released (:58, :65). Path A: ArchiveFileSystem.write :386 resolve -> archive X returned, then X.write(path) (OpenArchive.swift:825). Path B: evict :158-166 sees X.isBusy == false and removes X from slots/opened; the same happens at :70 when isCurrent() is false. Interleaving: B runs between A's resolve and A's openWriters += 1. Result: X is detached and gets pending changes. store.commit(url) :197 finds nil, or a second OpenArchive with nothing pending, and returns success. A mover (FileJob.swift:1155) then deletes its sources. flushAll at quit misses X and the scratch delete removes its spools. Only X's own timer can still save the data.
fix: Retire atomically: under X's L4, retireIfIdle() sets retired only if not busy; mutators throw a 'retired' error so ArchiveFileSystem re-resolves. Alternatively keep a store-level set of busy archives that the archive joins in changed()/write(), and have commit/flushAll iterate that.

title: Cancel is unresponsive on stalled I/O: several consumers pass neither a flag nor an interrupting tie and only poll between blocks (BUG 3).
detail: Affected: Packer.blocks (provider.read(item.url)), Packer.build, Unpacker.write, unpackAndOpen, openAsArchive, ArchiveFileSystem.read(_:) (opens a .member behind a long decompression with no way to interrupt), and timer and stop uploads.
fix: Use the cancellation variants plus monitor.cancellation.interrupting(...).

title: ArchivesPlugin.stop() runs a synchronous, uncancellable whole-archive rewrite or upload on main at quit.
detail: flushAll -> L2, L4, then flush() -> L5. rescueAll -> L5/L4. reportFailure (:107) asks directly, since already on main. store.close() runs archive deinits and a recursive scratch delete on main. flushAll and close deliberately never touch L3.
fix: See BUG 1 fix.

title: capabilities(for:) on main can wait behind rebase/takeSnapshot/install/finishWrite on L4.
detail: Takes L2 then L4, then the outer capabilities with nothing held. It never takes L5 or L3, so main cannot block behind a flush or a materialise, but it can wait behind rebase/takeSnapshot/install/finishWrite on L4.

title: ArchiveFileSystem.location(from:) does stat on main for typed paths.
detail: Listed under ArchiveCommands on main.

title: L3 (Slot.lock) is held across network round trips and whole opens, unbounded.
detail: While held: archive.isCurrent() :65 -> L4 then (L4 released, L3 still held) fileSystems.item(at: archiveURL) on the outer provider (OpenArchive.swift:491), a network round trip at most once per second with no cancellation; open() :72: remote/nested archive provider.item :119, provider.read :124, the whole download :130-133; OpenArchive.init -> load: ZIP directory parse, or a full decompress/bsdtar pass (archives <= 256 MB are materialised into a temp TAR up to 4 GB, OpenArchive.swift:353-366; larger ones stream-indexed end to end); evict :75: try() on other slots -> isBusy -> L4; deinit of the replaced archive (inside setArchive, :103); any user prompt the outer provider raises. Other threads wanting the same archive wait the whole prompt (unbounded at :56 without a flag).

title: L3 is held across askUser; safe only because main never takes L3, so any main-thread item/list/read/quarantine on that archive would deadlock.
detail: askPassword via ArchiveMemberReader init/read/seek holds no in-scope locks, except when the caller is ArchiveStore.open :124 reading an inner archive out of an encrypted outer ZIP: L3(inner) is held. Out-of-scope providers asking inside calls made from ArchiveStore.open :119/:124 and isCurrent OpenArchive.swift:491 hold L3.

title: reportFailure from the flush timer keeps its utility worker blocked in main.sync until the dialog is dismissed.
detail: On GCD utility (timer), no in-scope locks held (L4 released :761, L5 released by flush defer). The worker stays blocked until the dialog is dismissed.

title: If the CRC failure handler clears the password mid-run, every pool thread prompts separately, up to 3 attempts each.
detail: Low.

title: armTimer is a no-op while a retry or idleDelay timer (up to 60 s) is armed, so commit/move notifications and 'retry when something else changes' can lag up to 60 s.
detail: Minor.

title: Stale flush timers hold self strongly; after stop(), a retry timer can run flush against a deleted scratch folder and then block its worker in main.sync until exit.
detail: The closure holds self strongly, so an evicted archive's timer still fires. Harmless for notify-only timers. After stop(), a retry timer can run flush against a deleted scratch folder; it fails cleanly (atomic rename) and then blocks its worker in main.sync until exit.

title: scratch.removeAll() is serialised with in-table archives through L5 in flushAll, but not with detached archives (BUG 2) or post-stop timers.
flush() without leavingOutArrivals (timer, stop) writes members still under job temp names.
detail: Explicitly 'not a threading bug'.

title: Timer flush occupies a utility worker for a whole rewrite/upload and then indefinitely in reportFailure's main.sync; busy archives are uncapped (capacity 12 applies to idle ones only).
detail: GCD blocking / fan-out. One worker per failing archive.

title: Priority inversion: a userInitiated job in commit/move, or main in stop(), waits on L5 held by a utility-QoS worker.
detail: NSLock gives no priority donation.

title: Background.run blocks one userInitiated worker per unpack/test job; ProcessStream blocks one default-QoS worker per live child, including parked readers (up to 4 per archive, 10 s each).
detail: GCD blocking / fan-out.

title: Tool.filter uses two workers per bzip2 piece, about 2 x cores at once, possibly approaching GCD's blocked-thread limit on 24+ core machines.
detail: Speculation.

title: park schedules one 10 s asyncAfter per member read, so a 100k-member per-file copy out of a stream archive queues 100k blocks.
detail: Low.

title: timerFired polls every flushDelay (0.5 s) while any writer is open.
Deinit on main is possible for ArchiveMemberReader/OpenArchive when the last reference drops there; OpenArchive.deinit and ProcessStream.deinit run on arbitrary threads.
detail: The reader's closure holds the archive strongly. Deinits only unlink and terminate; ZipMemberWriter.deinit takes L4 briefly.

title: streamStarts is private(set) and readable unlocked (tests).
detail: Minor.

title: L4 (OpenArchive.lock) is held across stat, clonefile/unlink probe, access() x2, outer capabilities, scratch.newFile/createDirectory/open(O_CREAT), hasRoom/statfs, O(n log n) tree.ordered, install walk, and a full ZIP directory re-parse in rebase (longest hold, ~1 s on huge ZIPs).
detail: Notable L4 holders: isCurrent stat; timerFired idleDelay -> clones() clonefile + unlink probe (once); makeDirectory/write/remove/move/duplicate/setAttributes -> requireEditable -> access() x2 or fileSystems.capabilities(for:) on the outer provider (:685); write also environment.options (L1), scratch.newFile (L8 + createDirectory), open(O_CREAT); finishWrite hasRoom -> statfs, possibly volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage (:69, can be slow); takeSnapshot O(n log n) tree.ordered, clones(); install stat, open, rename, O(n) walk; rebase load(). Never held across askUser, a member read, or a flush.

title: L5 (flushLock) is held across whole-archive rewrite or outer-provider upload; for a nested archive it reaches outer L3, outer L4 and outer L5.
detail: build :1169: clone-append writes only pending bytes plus the directory; a rewrite copies the whole archive (multi-GB) plus copyfile xattrs. upload :1356: outer provider.write/move/item/remove for the entire archive; for nested archive reaches outer L3, outer L4 and outer L5 (via outer move -> flush), and outer ZipMemberWriter.drain -> Parallel.map. Not held: reportFailure, contentsChanged, askPassword.

title: Lock nesting order is acyclic as read.
detail: L3(inner) -> L3(outer); L3 -> L4 -> {L1, L8, L2 -> outer L4}; L5 -> L4; L5(inner) -> L3/L4/L5(outer); L7 -> L6 -> L10. L4 -> L5 does not exist (move :937 and timerFired :752 unlock first). L3(X) -> L5(X) and L5(X) -> L3(X) do not exist.

title: Lock leaf status: L1, L2, L6, L8, L9, L11 are leaves held for ns-us.
detail: ArchiveEnvironment.lock, ArchiveStore.lock, StreamInterrupt.lock (handlers run after unlock), ScratchFolder.lock, TemporaryFile.lock, SharedCounter.lock.

title: No NSCondition, DispatchSemaphore, NSRecursiveLock, private DispatchQueue, Thread, NotificationCenter, lazy var or @unchecked Sendable in scope.
Cancel on main is short.
detail: flag.cancel() -> StreamInterrupt.set (L6, L10 + terminate), InterruptSlot.interrupt (L7 -> L6 -> L10), outer reader/writer.interrupt().

title: capabilities(for:) never takes L5 or L3.
detail: Main cannot block behind a flush or a materialise.

title: ArchiveCommands on main avoid store.archive(at:).
detail: showMember, openAsArchive and unpackAndOpen use jobs; refreshOptions and open take only L1.

title: Only one flush at a time; no re-entry.
detail: L5 is a non-recursive NSLock; upload only calls outer providers.

title: Flush timer state machine is sound.
detail: timerFired clears timerArmed under L4 before flushing (:731), so a change during the flush arms a new timer (:712). Failure re-arms (:760). uploadPending and leavingOutArrivals walked; no state with pending changes and neither an armed timer nor an in-flight timer thread.

title: Writer close vs flush is sound.
detail: finishWrite and takeSnapshot are both under L4. The snapshot's records retain the spool TemporaryFile, so a concurrent remove cannot unlink it. install re-resolves entries by order. openWriters is balanced on every path (:834, :844, deinit :1457, close :1506/:1516).

title: Background.run has a happens-before.
detail: result is written in the group block and read only after group.wait returns success. tick runs on the caller.

title: Tool.filter has no pipe-fill deadlock.
detail: stdin written and stderr drained on GCD while the caller drains stdout; errors read after group.wait. F_SETNOSIGPIPE is set. Not cancellable, but the input is at most 4 MB.

title: ProcessStream is sound.
detail: stderr drained asynchronously and stdout by the reader; waitUntilExit runs only after EOF (:410). EOF depends on Foundation closing the parent's write end, which holds because the Pipe objects are passed directly.

title: Slot wait lock balance is correct.
detail: slot.lock.lock(before:) loop :52-54 registers the defer only after acquiring; try() at :158 and unlock at :168 are balanced.

title: ArchiveMemberReader.interrupt is safe at any time.
detail: Repeatedly, after close (current == nil), and alongside read/close. closeStream releases the slot before closing, and park re-checks control.isSet (:562).

title: ZipMemberWriter.interrupt is safe.
detail: StreamInterrupt.set; checked at write/drain/close; worst latency is one Parallel.map deflate window.

title: `.outside` forwarders return the outer provider's own reader/writer.
detail: interrupt() is native and the flag is forwarded wherever the protocol has one.

title: Internal interrupt consumers tie flags correctly.
detail: ArchiveStore.open :124-128 and upload :1362-1365 pass both the flag and flag.interrupting; the defer order releases the tie before reader.close().

title: Interrupt tokens use weak captures and live exactly the blocking span.
Every OpenArchive var is touched under L4.
detail: load runs in init or under L4 in rebase; clones() and canClone always under L4; ArchiveTree.ordered (mutating getter) always under L4. format is read unlocked at ArchiveFileSystem.swift:442 but assigned only in init.

title: Slot state and open-once logic are sound.
detail: Slot.archive/failure under L3 and lastUsed under L2. archive(at:) re-checks slots[key] === slot after taking L3 (:61-64), so two threads open one archive once, and a cancelled open removes its slot (:81-83).

title: ArchiveEnvironment closures are set once in start() before registration; Unpacker result/itemsDone/lines are job-thread only.
detail: Parallel.map bodies touch only SharedCounter, the monitor, and per-item streams.

title: No lock is held by any caller across Parallel.map.
detail: OpenArchive.swift:1488, Codecs.swift:584, Packer.swift:67, Unpacker.swift:96/:317. Bodies take L4 briefly, and L5 via provider.move into a ZIP; the caller holds neither.

title: Not read in full: ZipFormat.swift 1-299 and 390-514, ArchiveLocation.swift 131-286.
detail: Only grepped (no locks, queues, statics with state, or classes other than the streams there).

title: Nothing was built or run; every finding is from reading.
The network provider's write path was not traced beyond askUser for BUG 1.
